question: What important event is celebrated during the festival of 'Baisakhi' in Chandigarh?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Founding of Khalsa Panth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Baisakhi** is one of the most significant festivals celebrated in **Punjab** and particularly in Chandigarh, marking the formation of the **Khalsa Panth** by **Guru Gobind Singh Ji** on **April 13, 1699**.

• The **Khalsa Panth** was founded to instill unity and courage among the Sikh community and to uphold the principles of righteousness and justice.

• On this day, Guru Gobind Singh Ji initiated the **Panj Pyare** (The Five Beloved Ones), who symbolized the spirit of sacrifice and devotion to the Sikh faith.

• The festival also coincides with the traditional harvest festival in Punjab, marking the beginning of the **harvesting season** for crops like wheat.

• Sikhs visit **Gurdwaras**, participate in religious processions, and perform **Kirtans** and prayers, followed by community meals or **langars**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Significance of Khalsa Panth:**

• The **Khalsa** represents purity and dedication to the Sikh faith. Members of the Khalsa Panth are expected to follow the **Five Ks**: Kesh (uncut hair), Kara (iron bracelet), Kanga (wooden comb), Kachera (cotton undergarments), and Kirpan (ceremonial sword).

• The initiation into Khalsa Panth is marked by the **Amrit Sanchar ceremony**, where individuals commit to the principles of Sikhism.

• **Harvest Festival:**

• Baisakhi is celebrated as a **harvest festival** in Punjab, marking the end of the Rabi crop season and the start of the new agricultural year.

• Farmers express gratitude to God for a good harvest and pray for prosperity in the coming year.

• **Historical Context:**

• The founding of the Khalsa Panth was a response to the persecution faced by Sikhs and other communities under oppressive regimes, particularly during the Mughal era.

• Guru Gobind Singh Ji aimed to create a community of warriors and saints who would stand against injustice and protect the oppressed.

• **Other Celebrations:**

• Besides its religious significance, Baisakhi is celebrated with cultural activities like **Bhangra** and **Gidda** (traditional Punjabi dances).

• Fairs and processions are organized in various parts of Punjab and Chandigarh, attracting people from different communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Guru Gobind Singh Ji:** The 10th Sikh Guru, who played a pivotal role in shaping Sikhism and introduced the Khalsa tradition.

• **Panj Pyare:** The first five members of the Khalsa, representing the collective strength, unity, and commitment of the Sikh community.

• **Harvest Connection:** The festival aligns with the agricultural calendar, highlighting its importance in the agrarian society of Punjab.

• **Global Observance:** While primarily celebrated in India, Baisakhi is also observed by the Sikh diaspora worldwide, emphasizing its universal appeal within the Sikh faith.
